still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.
The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: 51.5% ever − 41.1% current = 10.4% of adults used and are off now; ~40% of current users are on a second or later course (16.4 pts), 3.2 pts cycled and are off again, so (16.4 + 3.2) / 51.5 ≈ 38.1% of ever-users have cycled; the remaining 7.2 pts stopped once and have not restarted. The cycled share fell from 40.5% because ~14 pts of first-time users joined (ever-used +14.0) and because persistence rose: low-dose calm, longevity, Reset and AUD plans (~24M licensed) persist ~55% at 12 months, and adherence-conditioned tracks persist ~60% because a premium differential or Medicaid eligibility rides on the fill record. Full-dose cash and gray weight users still persist about one-third; restart within a year 36–47%. Age check: 0.20×28 + 0.33×43 + 0.24×53 + 0.23×37.5 = 5.6 + 14.2 + 12.7 + 8.6 ≈ 41.1. Income thirds average ~41.0. 41.1% of ~276M adults ≈ 113.4M users, up ~36.7M. Payer mix: commercial ~22.0M (19%; ~14.0M of them in adherence-verified tracks), Medicare ~15.5M (14%), Medicaid ~4.6M (4%), legitimate cash ~43.0M (38%), gray ~28.3M (25%, up from 15.4M). Sum 113.4M. Legitimate cash: ~19.0M cash weight, ~11.0M metabolic/longevity, ~8.5M calm/focus, ~2.8M Reset, ~1.7M AUD fills = 43.0M. Gray: ~12.0M Indian generic semaglutide via registered B2C exporters and offshore telehealth, ~8.5M Chinese 'reta' and 'amy' (amycretin-sequence) vials, ~4.5M domestic unlicensed peptide clinics and 'personalised' compounders, ~3.3M counterfeit branded pens. About 26M users (~23%) have BMI under 30, ~9M under 25. Adult obesity ~30.4%. ~13% of adults have obesity and have never used, still concentrated in the rural South, the bottom third and 65+ without qualifying codes; most of the 7.2 pts who stopped once and stayed off cite GI effects, cost or, increasingly (~1 in 5 of 2035–36 stoppers), 'feeling flat' after the label change. Pediatric: ~1.3% of under-18s (12–17s ~3.0%, rising as conditioned family plans add adolescent dependants); 6–11 liraglutide ~0.10% after three more states joined the under-12 bans (fourteen states, ~38% of US children). ~62% of children live in a household with a current user; ~8M live with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~15.5M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 15.5M × ~$215 average net/month × 12 ≈ $40.0B gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up, up from ~$36.5B; average net fell $225 → $215. Dementia-risk route ~2.7M × ~$225 × 12 ≈ $7.3B. Medicaid: 10 states now cover weight-loss use; 6 of them (up from 2) condition coverage on verified adherence and BMI progress under 1115 waivers approved in Oct 2035. ~4.6M Medicaid users × ~$190 net × 12 ≈ $10.5B. Medicaid in the fourteen under-12 ban states does not pay for weight-indication use in that age group.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide $3–20 a month; since Jan 2035 about 400 exporters hold B2C export registration numbers, which they print on vials and storefronts. Chinese retatrutide- and amycretin-sequence vials $20–60 through research-peptide fronts. Canadian generic semaglutide CAD 40–70, Brazilian BRL 140–240. India and China supply ~72% of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Employer weight coverage rose 29% → 36% (Business Group on Health, Jan 2036), but ~90% of the new coverage requires verified adherence and BMI-progress milestones, and ~20% of large employers now run monitored metabolic tracks (up from 13%). Coverage widened only by becoming conditional. MariTide clinic administration anchors the tracks: ~8.0M clinic-administered of ~9.5M total MariTide users. Managed decline continued: MariTide cash $219 → $199; TrumpRx Wegovy pill maintenance $179 → $159, starting doses still $149; Foundayo $149–169; injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $199–249; Lilly cut retatrutide $299 → $269 for all doses. Amycretin list $1,199, still prior-authorised. Bimagrumab $1,150 list. Orals ~52% of users. Lifestyle spending accounts reimbursing calm/Reset platform fees spread from ~19% to ~27% of large employers. The gray market regrew around three structures: offshore-hosted telehealth platforms with non-US prescribers paired with Indian registered exporters (registration reads to buyers as a quality seal, though there is still no CBP mail agreement); domestic 'peptide clinics' and 'personalised' compounders operating without 503A/503B compliance in states with weak boards; and Chinese next-gen sequences ('reta', 'amy') sold to gym and longevity communities.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class and no new indication in this window. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial read out in mid-2035 (all-cause dementia HR ~0.86 in obesity plus CVD), keeping the existing indication; Lilly filed the non-CVD extension in Feb 2036 and it is under review, with no action before 2037. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 read out in Oct 2036, positive on its primary endpoint, with a filing planned for 2037; no compulsion indication exists. One Chinese GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist filed a US NDA in Sep 2036, so approval is impossible before late 2037. Implants are in phase 2. No oral matches tirzepatide. Brands hold $149–269 cash as US net prices drift down 3–5% a year. The 2035 class labelling of emotional blunting is a safety change, not an indication.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens; much lower on low-dose plans. Retatrutide 12 mg titration failure ~1 in 6. Gray 'reta' users report more severe GI events, consistent with dose variance.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; absolute cases up with volume; per-user risk unchanged.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation centres on EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; first EPI MDL bellwether tried in 2035 ended in a defence verdict; a second is set for 2037.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after 2+ years, ~1.45 after three or more cycles in 65+. Proportional lean loss similar in normal-weight users. Bimagrumab uptake is small (~0.4M) given price.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (2028) retained; DXA code in use; resistance-training label statements retained.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults, including in the anhedonia reanalysis, which found flattening without excess suicidality.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA pooled reanalysis (validated SHAPS/blunting scales from AUD, diabetes and weight trials plus the 2033 observational study) labelled in Apr 2035: clinically meaningful reduced reward response/emotional blunting in ~6% of patients at weight doses vs ~3% placebo, ~10% on retatrutide 12 mg, and ~4.5% vs ~3% at low doses (semaglutide ≤1 mg equivalent, oral ≤7 mg). Dose-related; resolves in most within 8 weeks of stopping. Gray microdose exposure is still unmeasured.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions 'Emotional blunting and reduced reward response' (Apr 2035) with prevalence figures and a recommendation to screen at follow-up. The FTC argues that platforms quoting the label as a benefit are deceptive; one case is pending.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months; fastest after retatrutide 12 mg and among gray users after seizures or bad batches. A new pattern: stoppers in adherence tracks lose the premium differential while they regain.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; underpins chronic-therapy framing and adherence conditioning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D; fat-soluble deficits with EPI; low ferritin in adolescent girls; gray longevity users rarely tested.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years); partial recovery in about half after 12+ months off. The tirzepatide 6-year excess is still non-significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling (2031); tirzepatide under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling; effects in people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~14 years of semaglutide follow-up. ~26M users with BMI under 30. The NIH normal-weight cohort enrolled ~40,000 by 2036; first data due 2038. No new confirmed signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth PMRs continue.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~71,000 by mid-2036. In Aug 2035 an endotoxin-contaminated 'reta' lot from a Phoenix-area peptide clinic hospitalised 64 people with sepsis-like reactions and killed 3. No repeat of the 2033 insulin-pen event at scale, but CDC counted ~300 further hypoglycaemia ED visits from counterfeit pens. Poison-centre calls ~9× 2025 levels. Registered Indian exporters test better than unregistered ones, but registration is not FDA approval.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts extended; four more state felony laws; FDA warning letters to 30 offshore telehealth domains, most of which reopened under new names. Federal personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 48-month liraglutide PMR update (2035) shows the ~0.7 cm/year deficit in prepubertal starters with early partial catch-up in a minority after stopping. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA label monitoring retained; no federal age restriction; fourteen state under-12 bans; EMA specialist initiation for 6–11.

food_and_beverage.state: About 58% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~17–19% from 2025, sugary drinks ~15%. Dollar sales are flat to slightly down. Zip-code assortment is universal. A counter-segment emerged: 'natty' and full-fat heritage lines (whole milk, lard-fried snacks, family-size bakery) sell well in low-density zips and among unmedicated 18–29s, partly offsetting multipack decline. Longevity supplements grow.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~21% from 2025, beer ~14%. AUD fills (~1.7M) and calm plans keep removing heavy drinkers. Two more regional brewers have consolidated. Natty bars and 'full-strength' craft rooms in Pittsburgh and Birmingham are a small bright spot.

restaurants.state: Traffic is down ~4% from 2034. Portion tiers and protein-forward menus are standard. Supper clubs that market large, shared, unmedicated meals ('Full Table') book out in Pittsburgh, Nashville and Portland. QSR late-night traffic tracks gray-supply interruptions in Memphis and the Delta.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Structured athletic and tailoring grow. A natty fashion line (soft workwear, high-waisted 'full-cut' denim) sells to the movement. Resale serves cyclers.

fitness.state: Strength and DXA-coaching grow. Employer tracks bundle gym check-ins as an adherence signal. 'Natty-verified' gyms (no incretins, verified by urine assay) open in Texas and Ohio, an ironic mirror of the verified tracks.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is 36%, almost all of the new coverage conditional. Pharmacy trend ~+8% as covered lives rise. Wellness and adherence-verification vendors are the fastest-growing benefits segment. Texas ERS and Ohio state employee plans adopted 30% adherence differentials in 2035. Part D premiums rose again.

pharma.state: Volume growth offsets price decline. Lilly leads on retatrutide; Novo on orals and low dose; Amgen on clinic-administered MariTide in employer tracks. Manufacturers do not promote blunting, but low-dose oral demand rose after the label change. Counterfeit and litigation spend ~$1.3B a year.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body reads as payment route, motive and now allegiance. Lean and scanned means covered and tracked. Lean with a daily pill means longevity. A monthly clinic bruise means the employer track. Regained means gray supply lost. A new reading: soft, strong and visibly eating means 'natty', unmedicated by choice, which signals defiance in Columbus and authenticity in Brooklyn.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Austin and Charlotte the status marker is still the biomarker printout. On the Columbus corridor and in Texas state agencies the tracked body is the price of a lower premium. In Georgia, Kentucky and four other states Medicaid enrollees must show monthly fills and BMI progress to keep coverage. Unmedicated identity is strongest among men 18–29 (on-drug 28%), evangelical fasting congregations and rural voters who could never pay; it is weakest in the middle-income 50–64 band, where 53% are on drug.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals in high-density zips are short and protein-led. The natty movement made large meals political: Sunday 'Full Table' suppers, church potlucks advertised as 'no shots at this table', and the Bread Alone network (~1,100 congregations) practising fasting without drugs. Family meals in mixed households are negotiated around who is on what.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'Natty' is now a dating-app filter alongside 'lean-mass verified'. Some apps sell assay-verified natty badges. Label language ('reduced reward response') is used in breakups. Couples on shared calm plans are common; mixed couples, one tracked and one natty, are the new counselling category.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier appetite is still noise to manage. Among the natty, appetite and intensity are proof of being 'yourself, full strength'. The movement fused Unmuted, MAHA-aligned parents, gym 'natty' culture and fasting churches, which disagree about almost everything except being unmedicated. Fat-acceptance activists remain wary, since the natty aesthetic prizes strength, not size.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Labelled Apr 2035: ~6% vs ~3% placebo at weight doses, ~10% on retatrutide 12 mg, ~4.5% vs ~3% at low doses. With ~113M users, about 3.6M excess cases at label rates (roughly 2.6M among weight-dose users and 1.0M among low-dose plan users); gray microdosing unmeasured. Platforms outside the 2034 consent orders quote the label figures as a benefit.
interior_life.framing: The label calls it an adverse reaction. Platforms such as Even and Plateau, which signed no consent order, sell 'label-confirmed reduced reward response' as calm, focus and freedom from craving. B2B vendors sell 'Steady' programmes to employers as productivity products, with the drug the 'clinical component'. Clinicians call it a dose-related side effect to screen for. The natty movement calls it sold sedation.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Adherence and calm are now explicitly bought: ~27% of large employers reimburse calm/Reset fees through LSAs, and ~14M workers are in adherence-verified tracks. 'Steady' vendors pitch lower attrition and fewer HR complaints. The Ohio ADA suit survived summary judgment in 2036 and is set for trial in 2037. Some unionised logistics sites negotiated opt-outs from the gym-check-in and mood check-in components but not from the premium differential.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Ambient and slow-game programming keeps growing for calm subscribers. Sportsbook handle per account is down ~20% from 2032 in high-density states. A natty counter-aesthetic (loud live music, 'full-strength' comedy nights, competitive eating revivals) fills rooms in Pittsburgh, Cleveland and Birmingham. The 'flat audience' remains a stand-up genre.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch is still the leading couples complaint; the label gave it a name partners use against each other. Some marketed calm plans now sell 'couples steadiness' bundles. Natty partners describe 'living with a label insert'.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2036 cycle made conditioning an issue: some House candidates took a 'natty pledge', and a Colorado ballot measure banning adherence-conditioned premiums and employment decisions passed in Nov 2036, effective 2027-style only from Jul 2037. Business lobbies defended the 30% guidance federally and held. The movement split votes across both parties, and there is still no turnout evidence of a 'sedated electorate'.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive on products, labelling-forward on safety, restrictive on the young, contested on marketing. The FDA labelled emotional blunting with prevalence figures (Apr 2035). The FTC sued one non-consent platform in late 2035 over feature marketing of the label; that case is pending. Three more states adopted under-12 bans (fourteen total). Congress passed nothing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No federal subsidy. Conditioning spread: CMS approved four more state 1115 waivers (six total) tying Medicaid incretin coverage to verified fills and BMI progress; Texas and Ohio state employee plans adopted 30% adherence differentials. TrumpRx continues at manufacturer-set prices. The 2027 tri-agency guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Fill records, clinic administrations, connected-scale weights, LSA claims and, since the label change, 'blunting screen' questionnaire scores flow to wellness vendors under consent. Vendors drop the blunting scores from employer dashboards after EEOC informal guidance (2036), but the fills and weights still go. Medicaid waiver states use cellular scales and pharmacy data to set eligibility.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE unchanged; the Army oral pilot continues. DOT's 2033 guidance stands, with a 2035 FMCSA advisory that examiners ask about blunting symptoms; gray use remains undisclosed by definition.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India's B2C export registration took effect Jan 2035; ~400 registered exporters, no CBP mail agreement, so registration functions as a marketing seal for US buyers. Chinese next-gen sequences move through research-peptide fronts. The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap is ~40–60×.

events.event: India's export registration for pharmaceutical parcels takes effect; registered exporters print registration numbers on semaglutide vials, and offshore telehealth sites pair with them to sell 'registered generic' plans to Americans for under $40 a month

FDA adds 'emotional blunting and reduced reward response' to the warnings on all incretin labels, citing about 6% of patients at weight-loss doses versus 3% on placebo and about 10% on high-dose retatrutide

Telehealth platforms not bound by the 2034 consent orders begin advertising 'label-confirmed calm'; licensed calm and focus subscriptions pass seven million by year-end, and the FTC sues one platform in November

CMS approves Medicaid waivers in four more states tying incretin coverage to verified monthly fills and BMI progress; Texas and Ohio state employee plans adopt the full 30% adherence premium differential
Employer survey finds 36% of employers now cover weight drugs, up from 29%, but nine in ten new plans pay only for workers whose adherence and weight progress are verified
Colorado voters approve a ballot measure banning adherence-conditioned premiums and job decisions from July 2037, backed by the 'natty' unmedicated movement, MAHA parents and labour groups

open_tensions: Coverage expanded only by becoming conditional: 14 million workers and Medicaid enrollees in six states hold their premiums or eligibility by staying on a drug whose label now warns of emotional blunting. The Ohio ADA trial in 2037 and Colorado's July 2037 ban will test whether that is lawful.

The label meant to warn about flattening became a sales sheet. The FTC's case against feature marketing is unresolved, calm plans have doubled, and the low-dose estimate of 4.5% versus 3% rests on thin data.

The gray market is larger and more organised than ever at ~28 million users, with Indian registration working as a quality seal and Chinese next-gen sequences in gyms; the Phoenix endotoxin cluster showed domestic peptide clinics are now part of the risk.

The unmedicated movement is a coalition of people who disagree about almost everything except refusing the drug, and it is entering a policy fight, over conditioning, where its strongest allies (labour) and its loudest voices (MAHA) want different things.

prose.headline: Label-Confirmed Calm: The Side Effect Became the Product, and Your Premium Depends on Taking It
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 about 113 million American adults take an incretin drug, more than two in five, and over half have tried one. The jump came from three directions at once. Employers began paying for the drugs again, but only for workers whose fills and weights are verified. Cheap generic vials came back through the mail, better organised than before. And the side effect people had complained about for years turned out to be something many would buy.

In April 2035 the FDA added emotional blunting to every incretin label, with numbers attached: about six patients in a hundred at weight-loss doses against three on placebo, ten in a hundred on high-dose retatrutide, slightly above placebo at low doses. The agency meant it as a warning. Within three months platforms that had never signed the 2034 consent orders were quoting it as a benefit. 'Label-confirmed calm' is now a phrase on subway posters. Licensed calm and focus plans have doubled to about eight and a half million subscribers. The FTC sued one company, and that case is still open.

Coverage widened by becoming conditional. Thirty-six percent of employers now cover weight drugs, up from twenty-nine, and nearly all of the new plans pay only when an app, a clinic or a connected scale confirms that the worker is taking the drug and losing weight. The 2027 rule allowing premiums thirty percent higher for unverified workers still stands, and Texas and Ohio applied it to their own state employees. Six state Medicaid programmes now require monthly fills and weight progress to keep coverage. Prices kept falling slowly, and only as the manufacturers chose. The Wegovy pill is $159 at maintenance on TrumpRx, MariTide $199, retatrutide $269. Starting pills are still $149, and the box still says $1,349.

The mail carries the rest. About twenty-eight million people use product that no American regulator approved. India's new export registration was supposed to tame the parcel trade, but without a customs agreement the registration number printed on each vial works mainly as a sales pitch. Offshore telehealth sites sell 'registered generic' plans for under forty dollars. Chinese copies of retatrutide and now amycretin circulate in gyms. In August 2035 a contaminated lot from an Arizona peptide clinic put sixty-four people in hospital and killed three.

The counter-movement calls itself natty, after the bodybuilders' word for drug-free. It is a coalition that does not agree with itself: young men who lift, fasting churches in the Bread Alone network, the Unmuted nights in Cleveland and Birmingham, and parents who cheered the under-twelve bans, now in fourteen states. Its members eat in public, and they eat a lot. Full Table supper clubs book out in Pittsburgh. Some gyms test urine to prove their members are drug-free, in the same way employers test adherence. In November Colorado voters banned adherence-conditioned premiums from July 2037, with labour unions and natty campaigners working together. Everywhere else the rule holds.

Work has absorbed it. Benefits vendors sell 'Steady' programmes that promise lower attrition. A former call-centre agent's disability suit in Ohio survived summary judgment and goes to trial next year. Sportsbooks report bettors wagering a fifth less per account than in 2032. Spirits volumes are down a fifth since 2025. Couples' therapists now hear partners quote the label insert to each other.

Nothing in the country is broken. Most people on the drug feel fine, and a few million feel less. The data that would show what years of low-dose use do to people who were never obese is due in 2038.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Vega gets to the clinic in Groveport at 6:40, before her shift, because the track counts the administration date and late is late. The nurse finds a spot on her abdomen that isn't still yellow from last month. MariTide, monthly. The app pings green: Verified. Her paycheck premium stays at $118 instead of $171.

At work she leads eleven agents on a returns queue. Her lead pay came through the same quarter as her ninth green month; nobody says those are related. The blunting questionnaire pops up on her phone at lunch. How often in the past two weeks have you enjoyed things you used to enjoy. She taps 'most days' because it is mostly true and because she doesn't know who reads it.

On the drive home a billboard on 270 says LABEL-CONFIRMED CALM, $89/MONTH, under a woman floating in a pool.

Dev's package is on the porch: a padded envelope from Ahmedabad, a registration number stamped on the customs slip, four vials. He stopped Zepbound when it went cash-only for him and started these in March. He keeps them in the butter door.

Their daughter, Lucía, sixteen, comes in with a pin on her backpack: NATTY. FULL STRENGTH. She eats two plates of arroz con pollo and watches her mother eat a third of one.

'Do you feel it?' Lucía asks. 'Like, any of it?'

Marisol thinks about it honestly. The dishes. The quiet. The green check.

'I feel fine,' she says, and Lucía writes that down, because she is collecting answers for a school project.
